title: Glossary & parent FAQ
lead: HL, SL, TOK, EE, CAS, AA, AI, diploma vs course results - in plain language.

hl-sl.body: Higher Level and Standard Level. A diploma has 3 or 4 HL subjects and the rest at SL; HL means more teaching hours and more depth.

tok.body: Theory of Knowledge: a core course about how knowledge is built. Graded A-E.

ee.body: Extended Essay: an independent research essay in a subject of the student's choice. Graded A-E.

cas.body: Creativity, Activity, Service: the non-graded core strand that must still be completed.

aa-ai.body: Analysis and Approaches leans to pure mathematics and proof; Applications and Interpretation leans to modelling and real-world data. Each comes at HL and SL.

diploma-vs-course.body: A student who does not meet the diploma conditions can still receive certificates for individual subjects (course results). It is a different outcome from the full diploma.

ue.body: New Zealand's minimum entry standard for university. For IB students it is a full diploma with at least 24 points, plus literacy and numeracy if studying in New Zealand.

myp-dp.body: The Middle Years Programme runs roughly Years 6-10; the Diploma Programme is Years 11-12. Subject choice for the DP is made in Year 10.

ncea.body: New Zealand's national secondary qualification, awarded at Levels 1, 2 and 3 - roughly Years 11, 12 and 13.

credits.body: NCEA is built from standards, each worth credits. A level needs 60 credits at that level or above.

co-requisite.body: A separate 20 credits (10 literacy + 10 numeracy) needed for any level of NCEA. Met once, counts for every level, and does not count towards the 60.

endorsement.body: Recognition of Merit or Excellence: 50 credits for a certificate endorsement; 14 credits in a course (with 3 internal and 3 external) for a course endorsement.

new-quals.body: The qualifications replacing NCEA from 2028 (Year 11), 2029 (Year 12) and 2030 (Year 13). The design is still being finalised.

ue-ncea.body: Four parts, all required: NCEA Level 3; 14 Level 3 credits in each of 3 approved subjects; 10 literacy credits at Level 2+; 10 numeracy credits at Level 1+.

when-to-choose.q: When do we actually choose subjects?
when-to-choose.a: In Year 10, the final MYP year. That is why this tool focuses on that decision.

how-many-hl.q: How many HL subjects are required?
how-many-hl.a: Three or four; the remaining subjects are SL, six in total.

can-change.q: Can subjects be changed after DP1 starts?
can-change.a: Sometimes early in DP1, but it gets harder quickly and depends on timetabling. Ask the IB coordinator immediately if you are considering it.

what-if-fail.q: What happens if the diploma conditions are not met?
what-if-fail.a: The student can still receive course results for individual subjects. Talk to the school about what that means for the applications you have in mind.

which-math.a: It depends on the target programmes. Most STEM and economics degrees expect AA. Check the requirements of each programme you are considering.

nz-vs-overseas.q: Does this plan work for overseas universities too?
nz-vs-overseas.a: The diploma structure is the same, but each country and university sets its own requirements. Use the pathway match as a starting point and verify on each university's own page.
